question: Should ClawHub allow post-publish changelog edits, and which roles, audit history, and public visibility rules should govern those edits?
rationale: The request is useful CLI ergonomics, but it mutates public release metadata that ClawHub presents as an install-time trust signal, so automation should not choose the policy boundary.

options.title: Specify audited owner edit workflow
options.body: Allow owners or publisher admins to edit changelogs only through an audited API/CLI path that updates denormalized latest summaries and preserves edit history.

options.title: Keep changelogs immutable
options.body: Reject post-publish edits and document that release-note corrections require publishing a replacement version.

options.title: Limit edits to staff repair
options.body: Permit only staff or moderators to correct release-note metadata for abuse, legal, or support cases while keeping publisher self-service immutable.

recommendation.title: Specify audited owner edit workflow
recommendation.body: Allow owners or publisher admins to edit changelogs only through an audited API/CLI path that updates denormalized latest summaries and preserves edit history.
